doc.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Festivals in Canada versus jazz parties
summary: Canada has festivals rather than jazz parties; he enjoys the social aspect of parties.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Good. These jazz parties that you come to, do they have such a thing in Canada?

Not really. Not in the same way. There was one gentleman who tried for a couple of years in Toronto. It didn’t quite work. The festivals seem to have a bigger impact in Canada. There are jazz festivals across the country from Halifax to Victoria, and unfortunately in a sense the jazz festival is about the only way that you can get to see some groups nowadays because of the economics. Although Toronto is very fortunate in that there’s a steady stream of great musicians passing through the city, we’re very lucky. There’s much more activity in Toronto year round than there is anyplace else in Canada.
How do you like playing with these rather — well kind of like semi-organized jam sessions, at the parties? Is it mostly enjoyable?

Oh yeah. We have a pretty good time. I think it shows. And it’s a relatively small circle of musicians and you establish friendships and so it becomes a pleasant social three or four days as well as musically stimulating too. So it’s nice.
